raw.assessment: The incumbent supports telephone and in-person booking, staffed key collection, and substantial recurring access: eleven groups obtained weekly bookings. Its strongest plausible account is that familiar human coordination serves most groups while preserving predictable reservations. It has not demonstrated the target: three conflicts occurred and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly; total needs and acceptable windows are unknown. A concrete limit on interpreting 68% reservation as spare usable capacity is the only acoustic piano: seven bookings required it, while other equipment needs were blank. Concentrated evening requests further limit substitutability. Late starts or absences do not establish that bookings could safely be reassigned.

openings.claim: Does unreserved capacity actually match unmet rehearsal needs once acceptable windows, duration, and equipment are recorded?
openings.delta: Distinguish allocation mismatch from scarcity of a particular room or time; aggregate utilization cannot make that distinction.
openings.prediction: An allocation mismatch would leave feasible assignments for previously unsuccessful groups; constrained scarcity would leave requests unmatched even after voluntary changes to inherited slots.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to record complete weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment, and the outstanding needs of groups rehearsing elsewhere. Attempt a paper allocation within existing hours and equipment, protecting both performances and every requested weekly 60-minute entitlement. Count matched stated needs without treating outside rehearsals or shortened sessions as substitutes without agreement.
assumptions: Contacts can describe group needs accurately.
Allocation is initially a feasibility exercise; any changes require confirmed agreement.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative desk calendar, booking identifiers, and recorded confirmation of every change would reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.delta: Replace independently actionable copies with one commitment record; retain the online calendar as a dated informational copy.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreements should cease causing conflicts; if duplicate arrivals persist despite matching confirmed identifiers, misunderstanding or another access process needs investigation. Administration may increase.
openings.probe: For two weeks, require volunteer and desk changes to reach the authoritative paper record before telephone or in-person confirmation; read back room, date, time, and identifier. Log conflicts, amendment effort, and whether participants relied on stale information. Continue only if the procedure supports the administration target.
assumptions: Existing telephone coordination can synchronize volunteer and desk without additional staffing.
Participants can retain a verbal or paper confirmation without an account.

raw.assessment: The observations establish unmet requests, uneven demand, unreliable access records and variable administration. They do not establish whether existing capacity can satisfy actual needs: acceptable alternatives, equipment requirements and total durations are missing. Recoverable slack remains a hypothesis.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: construct a weekly room calendar from protected 60-minute access entitlements plus additional rehearsal time, matching each group's declared acceptable windows, equipment and required uninterrupted duration instead of automatically inheriting 90-minute reservations.
openings.delta: The scheduling unit becomes a group's rehearsal requirement and minimum entitlement, rather than its previous reservation. Dependencies are complete requirements gathered by short conversations, fixed performance reservations, explicit acceptance of any shortened or separated sessions, and one authoritative desk record with confirmed updates to its copy. The presently testable partial capability is a manually constructed feasible calendar.
openings.prediction: If inherited reservation shapes and undisclosed alternatives cause some exclusions, a requirements-based draft will satisfy more stated rehearsal needs than the inherited calendar under identical capacity and performance commitments. If acceptable windows and equipment are too concentrated, the draft will expose remaining infeasibility.
openings.probe: Ask all twelve contacts for weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum uninterrupted duration. Compare inherited and manually reassigned calendars against those same requirements, protecting every requested weekly entitlement and both performances within the existing rooms and opening hours. Count full need satisfaction separately from minimum access. If feasible, confirm assignments by telephone or in person and track eight weeks of actual needs met, conflicts and all administrative minutes against the stated thresholds.
assumptions: Some groups accept alternatives or shorter sessions; this is unverified and must be elicited.
Additional time counts as useful only when it meets the group's declared rehearsal requirements.
Manual requirement collection and confirmation may exceed the administration budget; the probe must count that work.
The proposal uses existing equipment, introduces no fees, and requires no participant digital account.

openings.claim: Test whether requirement-based allocation improves usable access over inherited 90-minute bookings, distinguishing allocation mismatch from room/time scarcity.
openings.discriminator: Compare calendars against identical complete needs; distinguish full satisfaction from minimum access. Persistent unmatched piano/evening requirements indicate constrained scarcity.
openings.fit: Preserves two rooms, existing 24 staffed hours, requested weekly 60-minute entitlements, equipment, both performances, no new fees and telephone/in-person access without accounts. Changes require agreement; shortened, split or outside rehearsals count only if accepted.
openings.probe: Interview all twelve contacts about total weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment, uninterrupted duration and outstanding needs despite rehearsals elsewhere. Compare inherited and manually reassigned paper calendars. If feasible, confirm assignments through D2 and measure eight weeks of needs met, conflicts and all administration, including collection.
openings.uncertainty: Accurate contact reports and acceptable alternatives are unverified. Aggregate vacancy and late/absent bookings do not prove reclaimable usable time; administration may exceed budget.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk calendar, booking identifiers and confirmed changes may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.discriminator: Calendar-disagreement conflicts should cease; duplicate arrivals with matching confirmations implicate misunderstanding or another access process.
openings.fit: Preserves telephone/in-person booking and staffed key collection; online copy becomes dated information, with confirmed updates. No account or added staffing.
openings.probe: For two weeks, record volunteer/desk changes before confirming; read back room, date, time and identifier. Log conflicts, stale-copy reliance and amendment effort; retain only if administration supports the target.
openings.uncertainty: Existing coordination may not synchronize reliably; confirmation work may increase administration.

Merged with Z1; preserves requirement-based allocation and entitlement/full-need distinction; record dependency retained in D2.

post_distill.decision: Proceed with feasibility and record probes; success remains unestablished. Require at least 90% stated needs met within acceptable windows, fewer than two conflicts over eight weeks, and administration averaging at most 120 minutes weekly.
